notes: GT dataset contains only grain Zn concentration (mg/kg) observations; extraction data contains many other outcome types (yield, biomass, shoot Zn, root Zn, etc.) that must be filtered out.
GT zn_effect_rr appears to be log response ratio (ln(treatment/control)), range -0.62 to 1.43 is consistent with ln-scale.
Extraction ln_rr field should be used for effect size comparison rather than effect_pct.
GT n column is shared for both control and treatment (same replication assumed).
Many extraction papers contain non-Zn outcomes (yield in t/ha, biomass, shoot dry weight, etc.) that will contaminate matching if not filtered.
Paper 14_37_Liu_2019 appears to cover two studies (14 and 37) based on the compound ID; Liu_2014 may map to study 37.
Rashid_2019 and Ramzan_2020 both map to Pakistan studies; Rashid_2019 may be a separate study not in the mapping above.
Dong_2018, Li_2013, Liu_2014, Zhang_2017 are papers without numeric prefixes; their GT study_ids are estimated from context.
Unit mismatches are significant: many extraction observations use non-mg/kg units (t/ha, g/ha, %, etc.) that must be excluded or converted.
GT zn_ctrl range is 5.00 to 64.43 mg/kg and zn_treat range is 8.00 to 83.84 mg/kg, consistent with grain Zn concentration in mg/kg DW.

Extraction papers like 53_Grant_1998 have values in µg/kg (range 45-4540) which would need factor 0.001 to convert to mg/kg, but some values (45-4540 µg/kg = 0.045-4.54 mg/kg) seem too low; likely mixed units.
Papers 46_Ghasal_2017 and 65_Oliver_1994 appear to contain yield data (t/ha, US$/ha) rather than grain Zn; these may not contribute valid Zn observations.
The compound paper ID 14_37_Liu_2019 suggests it covers observations from two different GT studies (14 and 37).
